title: Component coproduct over prescribed dense opens
statement: Let X be a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and let ι_i:C_i→X, indexed by Fin(n), be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] from integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] whose images enumerate without repetitions the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. For dense opens V_i⊆C_i, there is a dense open U⊆X such that the component coproduct morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] restricted to U is an isomorphism and ι_i^{-1}(U)⊆V_i for every i.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, reduction to a dense disjoint union of components; expanded component-open proof in lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-component-modifications, steps 1-3 (Stacks web text checked)

proof.text: Set Z_i = range(ι_i) and W_i = complement of the union of the other irreducible components. The cover by Fin(n) makes the set of components finite, hence W_i is open. Mathlib closure_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff_singleton gives closure(W_i)=Z_i, so W_i is nonempty and contained in Z_i.

The restriction ι_i over W_i is a surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme, hence an isomorphism by Mathlib isIso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective. Transfer V_i intersected with the inverse image of W_i through this isomorphism to an open O_i of X. Density of V_i and nonemptiness of the open inverse image of W_i show O_i is nonempty. Since O_i is open, nonempty, and contained in the irreducible Z_i, closure(O_i)=Z_i. Further restriction shows ι_i restricted over O_i is an isomorphism.

Take U = union of O_i. The O_i are disjoint since W_i excludes every other component. Their closures are the components, which cover X, hence U is dense. The inverse image of U in C_i equals the inverse image of O_i and lies in V_i. FinitaryPreExtensive.isUniversal_finiteCoproducts identifies the coproduct of the restricted C_i with the restricted source of Sigma.desc ι. The restricted maps to U are open immersions with disjoint ranges covering U, so Mathlib nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of shows their coproduct is an isomorphism. The comparison equation and cancellation give the required isomorphism. The empty family works without a separate branch: hcover forces X empty and U is empty.

lean.statement: theorem exists_dense_open_component_coproduct (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X] (n : ℕ) (C : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (ι : ∀ i, C i ⟶ X) (hC : ∀ i, IsIntegral (C i) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (ι i) ∧ Set.range (ι i) ∈ irreducibleComponents X) (hinj : Function.Injective (fun i ↦ Set.range (ι i))) (hcover : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X, ∃ i, Set.range (ι i) = Z) (V : ∀ i, (C i).Opens) (hV : ∀ i, Dense (V i : Set (C i))) : ∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsIso (CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.desc ι ∣_ U) ∧ ∀ i, ι i ⁻¹ᵁ U ≤ V i
